[MUQATIL:80:1-7/r8] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The Prophet is not responsible if that man does not believe or mend what he corrupted; Muqatil applies this to the group of men.
[ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r4] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | The point is: what responsibility is yours if the person you invite to Islam does not accept it?
[SULAMI:v2p373#4/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · الواسطي | reports | Al-Wāsiṭī reads the phrase as treating with contempt the one who turns away.
[SULAMI:v2p373#4/r2] SULAMI, d. 412 · جعفر الخلدي | reports | Jaʿfar al-Khuldī says the Prophet was not honored by being directed toward someone God had not honored with guidance or shown gnosis.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r13] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The Prophet is not answerable if the other man is not purified; his duty is only to convey the message.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The whole passage is a reproach directed to the Prophet on behalf of the poor.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r2] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | The Prophet is not responsible if the man does not accept Islam; his duty is only to convey the message.
[JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4] JISHUMI, d. 494 · الحسن وجماعة | reports | They say it was revealed when Ibn Umm Maktūm interrupted the Prophet's effort to convert Meccan leaders; the Prophet turned back to them and God rebuked him.
[JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · الحسن وجماعة | reports | Afterward the Prophet honored him, welcomed him as the man over whom his Lord reproached him, and asked his needs.
[JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أنس | reports | Anas says he saw Ibn Umm Maktūm at al-Qādisiyya in armor with a black banner.
[JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · ابن زيد | reports | Ibn Zayd relates the saying that if the Messenger concealed revelation, he would have concealed this passage.
[JISHUMI:v10p7281/r13] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The Prophet bears no responsibility if the wealthy man does not accept Islam and purify himself from unbelief.
[JISHUMI:v10p7281/r14] JISHUMI, d. 494 · قيل | reports | Alternatively, the question means ‘Would it grieve you if he did not accept Islam?’ His unbelief cannot harm the Prophet, whose duty is only to convey.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r8] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The phrase means that the person may not believe or be guided; the Prophet's duty is only to convey the message.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r12] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The phrase means that it would not harm or concern the Prophet if the wealthy man failed to purify himself or prosper; it urges him not to concern himself with them.
[TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r12] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The Prophet bears no responsibility if the wealthy man does not accept Islam and leave disbelief; his duty is only to convey.
[TABRISI:80:20/r10] TABRISI, d. 548 · المرتضى علم الهدى | rejects | Al-Murtada rejects identifying the passage's subject as the Prophet: the text does not name him, and frowning at a believing seeker or preferring rich people to the poor conflicts with his noble character.
[TABRISI:80:20/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | The passage is said to have been revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum, also named Abdullah ibn Shurayh ibn Malik ibn Rabiʿa al-Fihri, when he came as the Prophet was urging Quraysh leaders toward Islam.
[TABRISI:80:20/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | The Prophet was speaking with ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa, Abu Jahl, al-ʿAbbas, Ubayy, and Umayya ibn Khalaf when Ibn Umm Maktum repeatedly asked to be taught; the Prophet turned away, thinking the leaders might scorn a following of blind people and slaves.
[TABRISI:80:20/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Afterward the Prophet honored Ibn Umm Maktum, greeted him as the man for whom his Lord had reproached him, asked about his needs, and appointed him deputy in Medina twice.
[TABRISI:80:20/r9] TABRISI, d. 548 · أنس بن مالك | reports | Anas ibn Malik says he saw Ibn Umm Maktum at al-Qadisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black standard.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | You bear no responsibility if the person you invite to Islam does not accept it; your duty is only to convey the message.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p52#4/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | You are not responsible if the person you call does not accept Islam; your duty is only to convey, so zeal for their conversion must not turn you away from a believer.
[QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The unbeliever's failure to be guided or believe is not the Prophet's responsibility; he is responsible only for conveying the message.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r10] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The point agrees with the statement that the Messenger's duty is only to convey the message. | mentions 42:48
[BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r9] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The Prophet is not accountable if the man does not convert; eagerness for his Islam should not cause neglect of one who has accepted it.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#5/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The Prophet is not responsible for making the man accept Islam and purify himself; his duty is only to deliver the message.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The phrase diminishes the unbeliever's importance and urges the Prophet to stop attending to him: it is no concern if he fails to prosper or purify himself of disbelief.
[SAMIN-DURR:80:7/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | ألا يزكى is the subject, and عليك is its predicate: the man’s failure to purify himself is not your responsibility.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The self-sufficient person is the rich man whom the Prophet approached in hope of guidance, though he was not accountable if the man failed to purify himself.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing. | mentions 79:45
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Luxury and self-sufficiency signal rejection and readiness for disbelief and wrongdoing; affliction can purify, humble, and soften hearts, so the more deeply tried are more receptive to fear.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · أبو جعفر بن الزبير | reports | Ibn al-Zubayr connects this opening to the prior calls to heed and fear: humble people whom the world overlooks are especially cared for and chosen by God. | mentions 79:26, 79:45
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The saying that a disheveled, dusty person whom people ignore could swear an oath that God would fulfill illustrates the hidden rank of the humble.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | reports | Ibn Umm Maktūm was the Prophet’s muezzin and the man whose visit occasioned the sūra’s admonition.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The rebuke teaches the Prophet to remain patiently with people like Ibn Maktūm and not to despise them, echoing other admonitions and the command not to drive away those who seek God. | mentions 18:28, 39:65, 38:88, 31:18
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Ibn Maktūm sought instruction while the Prophet addressed a Quraysh notable whose conversion he hoped would save the man and his kin; attending to that hope led him to neglect the immediate visitor.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | A preceding citation of 6:52 praises God’s kindness to His servants and prays not to be cut off from His mercy. | mentions 6:52
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The Prophet bears no blame if the proud man fails to purify himself, even minimally; his duty is only to convey the message.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | reports | The wording may also be parsed as a question: what burden would fall on the Prophet if the man were not purified?
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | One should still strive to purify a follower when there is reason to expect that he will accept guidance.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r9] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The passage uses ḥtibāk: mentioning the rich first implies the poor second, while the seeker’s coming and fear imply their opposites in the first case.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The description of the Prophet as a warner to those who fear applies to Ibn Umm Maktūm. | mentions 79:45
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The command to keep company with those who call upon God morning and evening is another passage revealed in the pattern of Ibn Umm Maktūm’s case. | mentions 18:28
[DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · عائشة | reports | In another account, ʿAʾisha says the Prophet was addressing Quraysh leaders including Abu Jahl and ʿUtba when Ibn Umm Maktum came; the Prophet turned away, and the quoted passage was revealed. | mentions 80:5, 80:6, 80:7, 80:8, 80:9, 80:10
[BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r11] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The Prophet bears no blame or burden if the self-satisfied man does not become purified by Islam; there is no need to prioritize him over someone who has accepted guidance.
[BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r12] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | One should not press Islam upon a person with no receptivity who loves the present world and is blind to the hereafter; the verse also belittles the one who turns away.
[BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r13] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Mā is negative; the implied preposition fī is linked to an omitted noun, and the clause is circumstantial to taṣaddā, reinforcing the rebuke.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p41/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The Prophet bears no blame if the

disbeliever does not purify himself; eagerness for his conversion should not cause the Prophet to turn away from someone who has believed.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p41/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Ma is negative and the clause is circumstantial from the subject of taṣaddā; alternatively it is an interrogative repudiation meaning the same thing: what harm is it if he does not purify himself?
[ELMALILI:80:3-42/r6] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | The Prophet bears no responsibility if the self-sufficient person refuses purification or Islam, but ignoring a Muslim who seeks instruction entails responsibility; guidance efforts toward unbelievers remain permissible in principle.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r8] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Mā is negative; ʿalayka is the fronted predicate and allā yazakkā is the subject.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r9] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The Prophet is not responsible for the man’s failure to purify himself and need not exert himself beyond what God requires; this is divine gentleness toward His Messenger.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r8] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Mā is negative; ʿalayka is the fronted predicate, and the clause “that he be purified” is the delayed subject.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r9] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The man’s failure to be guided is not the Prophet’s responsibility; he is not accountable for it and need not press beyond what God charged him with. This reassures him.
[TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | rejects | The proposed honorific reading of the switch from third to second person does not fit the direct address that follows, whose rebuke is stronger and has no conciliatory intimacy.
[TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The rebuked pattern is that the Prophet attends to wealthy people who scorn the truth, unconcerned whether they purify themselves, while neglecting the person earnestly seeking purification and fearing God.
[TABATABAI:80:5-12/r6] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · قيل | reports | One reading takes mā as negative: it is no fault of yours if the rich man does not purify himself, so eagerness for his conversion should not divert you from one who already accepted Islam.
[TABATABAI:80:5-12/r7] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · قيل | reports | A second reading takes mā as an incredulous question: what obligation falls on you if he does not cleanse himself of disbelief and sin? You are only a messenger responsible for conveying.
[TABATABAI:80:5-12/r8] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | prefers | The most contextually apt reading is that the Prophet should not concern himself with the rich man's failure to purify himself; the interrogative reading comes next, and the negative reading is least apt.
[ASAD-NOTES:80:3#n3/r1] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | Asad's literal gloss says it is not upon the Prophet if the man does not attain purity.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | ʿAbasa pairs with al-Nāziʿāt and shares its central theme, discourse style, and reasoning; the changed sequence of topics gives this sūrah its distinct majesty. | mentions 79:45
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r5] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The Prophet’s duty is to warn of the Hereafter and communicate Islam, not to ensure that people become Muslims or to overburden himself over their refusal.

<<end of notes>>
